literal: Five he-who-subdued power wide sky those-who-are king Indra-himself is-sufficient witness.
translation: Indra himself, the king of those in the wide heaven, is sufficient witness to the power of one who has subdued the five senses.
modern: ஐம்புலன்களையும் அடக்கியவனின் வலிமைக்கு, அகன்ற வானத்தில் வாழ்பவர்களின் அரசனான இந்திரனே போதுமான சாட்சி ஆவான்.
explanation: This couplet illustrates the immense power of an ascetic who has completely mastered their senses. The word 'ஐந்து' (five) implicitly refers to the desires arising from the five senses, and 'அவித்தான்' means one who has extinguished or subdued them. The word 'கரி' has multiple meanings such as elephant or charcoal, but here it takes the specific meaning of 'witness' or 'evidence'. Even Indra, the mighty ruler of the celestial beings in the vast heavens, serves as a sufficient witness ('சாலும் கரி') to the superior strength of a true ascetic, showing that spiritual discipline surpasses celestial authority.
